title: Named Mainz, Olomouc, German, Hungarian, Adriatic, Utrecht and Riga book witnesses

traditions.label: Mainz Mass-book witnesses
traditions.scope: A medieval summer-part manuscript and one identified Mainz print, not the whole printed series.
traditions.coverage_note: The 1482 book is not made an immediate successor to the Frankfurt manuscript; other dated prints need independent collation.

traditions.label: Olomouc Mass-book witnesses
traditions.scope: Named 1488 print and a surviving fragment of the 1499 print.
traditions.coverage_note: The 1499 fragment cannot characterize the whole edition or demonstrate a new recension.

traditions.label: Augsburg diocesan Missal
traditions.scope: The 1510 Augsburg print, distinct from similarly named Aosta books.
traditions.coverage_note: Earlier and later Augsburg printings require comparison; the title mentions added Masses without dating their introduction.

traditions.label: Bamberg diocesan Missal
traditions.scope: The 1490 Bamberg print identified by its title and colophon.
traditions.coverage_note: Its episcopal preface is indexed, but the instrument and other prints have not been collated.

traditions.label: Bremen diocesan Missal
traditions.scope: The 1511 Bremen print, not a claim about every Bremen manuscript.
traditions.coverage_note: Two fifteenth-century manuscript leads remain uncollated against the print.

traditions.label: Eichstätt diocesan Missal
traditions.coverage_note: The indexed episcopal text and rubrics are bounded contents evidence, not a reviewed reform.

traditions.label: Pécs Mass-book print
traditions.scope: The 1487 Missale Quinqueecclesiense identified in a Wolfenbüttel copy.
traditions.coverage_note: A later handwritten title is explicitly misleading; the 1499 print and fragments remain separate evidence.

traditions.label: Eger-held Mass-book and Eger ordinal
traditions.scope: A dated missal manuscript now held at Eger and a separate 1509 Eger ordinal component.
traditions.coverage_note: Miskolc use is uncertain from the scribe name; an ordinal is not a complete Mass book.

traditions.label: Zadar Franciscan gradual-missal
traditions.scope: A thirteenth-century OFM gradual-missal, separate from a secular Zadar diocesan use.
traditions.coverage_note: The catalogue attribution and manuscript contents support a bounded OFM state, not a diocesan recension.

traditions.label: Split manuscript leads
traditions.scope: The Split cathedral missal, its older sacramentary fragments, and a disputed Dalmatian manuscript attribution.
traditions.coverage_note: No secure single dated Split book-state row is promoted here; layers and origin need examination.

traditions.label: Utrecht diocesan Missal
traditions.scope: The 1495 Delft printing titled for the Utrecht ordinal.
traditions.coverage_note: Other Delft and later prints need collation; Old Catholic reception is outside this witness claim.

traditions.label: Riga Mass-book manuscript
traditions.scope: Akad. Rīga Ms. 1 (R 2665), catalogued as Missale Rigense.
traditions.coverage_note: The c.1450 catalogue dating conflicts with another institutional fourteenth-century account; an exact copying bound is not settled.

sources.title: Usuarium book 5594, Missale Moguntinum
sources.inspection: Book identity fields read: 1030–1070, UB Frankfurt Ms. Barth. 118, pars aestivalis.
sources.limitations: Research catalogue, not inspected original manuscript images.

sources.title: Usuarium book 28, Missale Moguntinum
sources.inspection: Book card title, 1482 age, Würzburg printer, BSB Rar. 0957, and contents rows 7, 9, 27, 257 and 437 read.
sources.limitations: Index and transcription of headings are not direct collation of original body or episcopal instrument.

sources.title: Landesbibliothekszentrum Rheinland-Pfalz, Missale Olomucense
sources.inspection: Institutional digitisation record read: Bamberg, Sensenschmidt for Drach, 4 March 1488, 370 leaves, original holding link.
sources.limitations: Edition-identifying metadata; original leaves and Mass contents not independently collated.

sources.title: Usuarium book 122, Missale Olomucense
sources.inspection: Book card read: 1499 Nuremberg Stuchs print, BSB 2 Inc.c.a. 3786 m, explicitly a fragment; sole indexed sanctoral page 4 (268r).
sources.limitations: The surviving fragment does not attest the rest of the book or a complete 1499 recension.

sources.title: Usuarium book 19, Missale Augustense
sources.inspection: Book card and rows 4, 6, 8, 30, 217, 302, 446, 458 and 484 inspected: 1510 Ratdolt print, BSB 2 Liturg. 185 a.
sources.limitations: Catalogue headings and title claim of added Masses are not a text collation or date of each addition.

sources.title: Usuarium book 20, Missale Bambergense
sources.inspection: Book card and rows 19, 21, 330, 341, 439 and 645 read: Sensenschmidt 1490, BSB 2 Inc.c.a. 2432.
sources.limitations: Indexed decree and colophon have not been checked against original page images.

sources.title: Usuarium book 106, Missale Bremense
sources.inspection: Book card and contents rows 10, 218, 246, 351 and 452 read: 1511 Strasbourg Beck print, BL b.52.h.4.
sources.limitations: Catalogue identification and headings, not an original-page collation or evidence of citywide reception.

sources.title: Usuarium book 22, Missale Eystetense
sources.inspection: Book card and rows 10, 16, 326, 374 and 516 read: 1486 Reyser print, BSB Rar. 0953.
sources.limitations: Episcopal text and local rubrics are indexed, but their full wording and earlier comparison are uninspected.

sources.title: Usuarium book 91, Missale Quinqueecclesiense
sources.inspection: Book card and rows 19, 253, 267, 392 and 609 read; 1487 Wenssler print, HAB H:S 456.2° Helmst.; warning about later handwritten mislabel read.
sources.limitations: Contents index only; handwritten label is not accepted as original title or place of use.

sources.title: Usuarium book 764, Missale Miskolci
sources.inspection: Book card, 1394 colophon transcription and rows 18, 164, 170, 242 and 367 read; Eger U2 VI.5 holding.
sources.limitations: Catalogue expressly doubts Miskolc origin; original colophon image and locale of use uninspected.

sources.title: Usuarium book 854, Ordinarius Agriensis
sources.inspection: Book card read: 1509 Kraków Haller ordinal, Ossolineum XVI.Qu.1922, modern Dobszay edition separately identified.
sources.limitations: An ordinal gives directions, not all prayers; exact Eucharistic sections and original leaves remain uninspected.

sources.title: Usuarium book 1132, Missale Iadrense
sources.inspection: Book card read: BAV Reg. lat. 2049, 1250–1300, OFM Zadar; contents rows 11, 22, 219, 226 and 313, with Vatican digitisation link.
sources.limitations: Research catalogue and indexed headings, not a direct folio collation; OFM context must not become secular diocesan use.

sources.title: Usuarium book 96, Missale Traiectense
sources.inspection: Book card read: original title, 1495 Snellaert Delft print, KB Den Haag 170 E 11; contents rows 10, 18, 258, 269, 346 and 534.
sources.limitations: Catalogue headings and colophon index do not establish a distinct recension relative to other Utrecht prints.

sources.title: Usuarium book 560, Missale Rigense
sources.inspection: Book card read: Ms. 1 (R 2665), approximate 1450 date and provenance-note transcription; contents rows 4, 10, 209, 214 and 281.
sources.limitations: Approximate catalogue date conflicts with another reported dating; provenance note and marginal layers require original-folio review.

stages.label: Frankfurt Ms. Barth. 118, summer Missal part
stages.witness_label: Frankfurt Ms. Barth. 118, summer Missal part
stages.summary: The 1030–1070 range is a catalogue copying estimate, not duration of Mainz use.

evidence.claim: A Mainz-attributed summer-part missal manuscript is catalogued at Frankfurt.

stages.limitations: No full contents, reception or relationship to later prints established.
stages.reception: Local use and original production site are not independently proved.

stages.label: 1482 Missale Moguntinum, BSB Rar. 0957
stages.scope: Single Mainz print, not the whole series.
stages.summary: The 1482 date belongs to Reyser’s printing; the indexed prefatory item is not treated as an independently verified act.

evidence.claim: The print is identified and indexed with episcopal prefatory text, calendar, temporal, Canon and sanctoral.

stages.limitations: Original leaves and the remaining printed series are uncollated.
stages.reception: No 1482 diocesan adoption or direct descent from Ms. Barth. 118 asserted.

stages.label: 1488 Missale Olomucense, Bamberg
stages.scope: One edition-identified print; component contents are not certified.
stages.summary: This is the publication date of the Sensenschmidt/Drach book.

evidence.locus: Digitisation title record, Published and Description fields
evidence.claim: The holding library identifies an Olomouc Missal edition of 4 March 1488, 370 leaves.

stages.limitations: The print was not collated against Olomouc manuscripts or the later prints.
stages.reception: A title for Olomouc does not date first or universal diocesan use.

stages.label: 1499 Missale Olomucense surviving fragment
stages.summary: The date identifies the edition; the surviving fragment does not stand for its complete contents.

evidence.locus: Book 122, age, shelfmark, Remark Fragment and p. 4 (268r)
evidence.claim: The Nuremberg Stuchs print is identified by a surviving BSB fragment with a sanctoral entry.

stages.limitations: The date and single indexed leaf do not prove change from 1488.

stages.label: 1510 Missale secundum ritum Augustensis ecclesiae
stages.scope: One 1510 Augsburg book; title-level additions only.
stages.summary: Ratdolt’s print is dated 1510, while introduction dates of its named additions are unknown.

evidence.claim: The named Augsburg print contains indexed episcopal prefatory text, calendar, Ordinary and Mass divisions; title mentions added Masses.

stages.limitations: The title’s added-Masses language is not encoded as a before/after transition.
stages.reception: The indexed episcopal preface does not by itself establish dates or extent of diocesan implementation.

stages.label: 1490 Liber missalis Bambergensis
stages.summary: Its title names Bamberg order, and the index locates a bishop’s prefatory item.

evidence.claim: The Sensenschmidt book is identified by the 1490 colophon and indexed Mass sections.

stages.limitations: No comparison with the 1499 or 1507 print, and no inferred reform.
stages.reception: Printing for the Bamberg church is distinct from proved use in every local parish.

stages.label: 1511 Ordo missalis Bremensis

evidence.claim: The Strasbourg Beck print names Bremen order and contains indexed temporal, Ordinary, Canon, sanctoral and Common.

stages.limitations: Fifteenth-century Bremen manuscripts and this print remain uncollated.
stages.reception: No date of Bremen-wide reception inferred.

stages.label: 1486 Missale Eystetense
stages.summary: The date marks publication of BSB Rar. 0953.

evidence.claim: The Reyser print is identified with indexed diocesan prefatory text, Ordinary, sanctoral and local rubrics.

stages.limitations: The bishop’s text is an indexed item, not an inspected full instrument; no precursor comparison.
stages.reception: No first-use or later replacement date established.

stages.label: 1487 Missale Quinqueecclesiense, Wolfenbüttel copy
stages.scope: One 1487 print despite its later misleading handwritten label.
stages.summary: The source expressly warns that the later Ultramontanorum tag is incorrect.

evidence.locus: Book 91, age, remark and contents pp. 19, 253, 267, 392
evidence.claim: The Basel Wenssler print is attributed to Pécs, with indexed temporal, Ordinary, Canon and sanctoral material.

stages.limitations: Original print has not been collated with 1499 or manuscript fragments.
stages.reception: Attribution of the book is not proof of every parish’s use.

stages.label: Eger U2 VI.5, 1394 missal manuscript
stages.scope: Dated manuscript identity, not a certified Miskolc or Eger local recension.
stages.summary: The year is a scribal colophon date reported by the catalogue.

evidence.locus: Book 764, colophon Remark and contents pp. 18, 164, 170, 242, 367
evidence.claim: A colophon names scribe Ladislaus de Miskolch and year 1394; the manuscript is held at Eger.

stages.limitations: The scribe name alone does not determine production or use place.
stages.reception: Eger holding does not establish historical Eger diocesan reception.

stages.label: 1509 Ordinarius Agriensis component
stages.summary: Its 1509 date is publication, while the modern Dobszay edition is separate.

evidence.locus: Book 854, original title, genre, age and holding fields
evidence.claim: The Haller print is identified as an Eger ordinal for observance, distinct from a missal.

stages.limitations: Exact Mass-specific provisions and relation to 1514 print not checked here.
stages.reception: Title’s Eger association does not give implementation date.

stages.label: BAV Reg. lat. 2049, Zadar OFM gradual-missal
stages.scope: One Franciscan manuscript, not a Zadar cathedral missal.
stages.witness_label: BAV Reg. lat. 2049, Zadar OFM gradual-missal
stages.summary: The range is estimated copying date, not duration of Franciscan use.

evidence.claim: The manuscript is indexed as a gradual and missal with a Roman-curial order title and Mass components in Franciscan Zadar context.

stages.limitations: Original leaves and possible later layers are uncollated.
stages.reception: The OFM attribution does not establish a separate secular Zadar recension.

stages.label: 1495 Missale secundum ordinarium Traiectensem
stages.summary: The 1495 date is a print date, not a new Utrecht rite event.

evidence.claim: The Snellaert Delft print names the Utrecht ordinal and is indexed with the major Mass divisions and colophon.

stages.limitations: Other Utrecht manuscripts and prints remain uncollated.
stages.reception: No relation to modern Old Catholic books or adoption date is asserted.

stages.label: Akad. Rīga Ms. 1 (R 2665), Missale Rigense
stages.date_label: c.1450 catalogue estimate; competing fourteenth-century dating unresolved
stages.scope: One manuscript with reported provenance and marginal notes.
stages.summary: The catalogue identifies one Riga missal with indexed Mass contents and a reported cathedral altar ownership note. Its copying date is left unpositioned pending reconciliation of divergent estimates.

evidence.locus: Book 560, age, shelfmark, fol. 2 note and contents pp. 4, 10, 209, 214, 281
evidence.claim: The catalogue identifies one Riga missal with indexed Mass contents and a reported cathedral altar ownership note.

stages.limitations: Ownership transcription and manuscript layers need original-folio review; this is not the Viborg print held in Riga.
stages.reception: The altar note is ownership context, not an independently established date of general Riga adoption.
